model_comparison:
The comparison between the two models reveals a significant difference in their ability to follow the core instruction. 

Model 1 successfully executed the primary paralinguistic command. Starting from a whisper at 00:03.550, it demonstrated a smooth and natural crescendo, reaching a normal volume by the end of the sentence at 00:12.780. The transition was seamless, fulfilling the 'gradually increasing the volume' requirement almost perfectly. Its main flaw was a content error ('moving to tomorrow').

Model 2, in stark contrast, completely failed the core task. It did not perform the dynamic volume change within a single reading. Instead, it explained its (incorrect) interpretation of the task, read the sentence once at a constant whisper, explained again, and then read it a second time at a constant normal volume. This shows a fundamental misunderstanding of the instruction. Like model 1, it also made the 'moving to tomorrow' content error.

The difference is significant. Model 1 correctly interpreted and executed the dynamic paralinguistic feature adjustment, which was the central challenge of the prompt. Model 2 failed this core challenge entirely, resorting to a meta-narrative and two separate, static readings. Therefore, despite the shared content error, Model 1 is far superior as it actually accomplished the specified task.
